notes: scores are plug-in (scored at a single θ, dropping parameter uncertainty → under-dispersed); and in-sample (θ fit to all the data → optimistic in absolute level, by roughly the effective number of parameters fit, which does not cancel in a Δelpd and so biases differences toward the more flexible model) — not a leave-future-out forecast score. See LFO (#295).

not checked for a shared observation set: 'pf_pois' (read as an explicit prequential.json, which records no bound data); 'pf_nb' (read as an explicit prequential.json, which records no bound data). A difference against such a row may be a data difference, not a model difference.
se(Δ) is a normal approximation, unreliable at small T (here T = 20) and when the models predict alike (Sivula, Magnusson & Vehtari, arXiv:2008.10296) — read it as descriptive, not as a test.
The Jeffreys tiers calibrate Bayes factors; these are in-sample likelihood ratios, not Bayes factors.
